candidate_relations.reason: The pathology demonstrates pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei in a myxochondroid matrix with S100 positivity and low MIB-1, cartilaginous gross specimen (tan-brown rubbery with cartilage), and binucleate forms without mitoses — all consistent with low-grade chondrosarcoma. Schwannoma is a peripheral nerve sheath tumor with distinct histology (Antoni A/B patterns, Verocay bodies) and would not produce a myxochondroid matrix or cartilaginous gross specimen. While S100 positivity is shared, the myxochondroid stroma, pleomorphic nuclei, and cartilaginous gross appearance are defining features of chondrosarcoma, not schwannoma. The anatomical location (mastoid near stylomastoid foramen with fallopian canal expansion) could fit either, but histology decisively excludes schwannoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Schwannoma vs. low-grade chondrosarcoma; different histological entity entirely

case_quality_flags: S100 positivity is present in both schwannoma and chondrosarcoma; differentiation relies on myxochondroid matrix and cartilaginous gross pathology favoring chondrosarcoma
KI-67/MIB-1 negativity/low index supports low-grade designation
